title: How much of the tank does the tap fill?
description: A tap fills seven tenths of a tank in one hour. The part filled in four shorter times is found by multiplying, and the time for a full tank is found last.
teaching_notes: One idea: a part of an hour fills that same part of the hour's amount, so we multiply and shorten before multiplying. Watch for students who add the fractions instead of multiplying them.

video_script.why: The child uses the multiply and shorten method of the solved example on a tap filling a tank.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question, a tap that fills seven tenths of a tank in one hour
video_script.anchor: a water tank with seven tenths shaded, labelled one hour
video_script.payoff_line: The full tank needs ten sevenths of an hour
video_script.fraction_reading: one third, two thirds, three quarters, seven tenths, seven thirtieths, seven fifteenths, twenty one fortieths, forty nine hundredths, ten sevenths
maths_rules: (b) 2/3 × 7/10 = 14/30 = 7/15 (2 is a common factor of 14 and 30)
(e) 7/10 × 1/7 = 1/10, so the full tank takes 10 × 1/7 = 10/7 hours = 1 3/7 hours
check: 3 × 7/30 = 7/10, the amount for one hour
video_script.design: A tank with seven tenths shaded for one hour. Each time is a shorter part of the hour; the working board shows one product per line.
open_questions: The book key prints (b) as 14/30; the worklist shortens it to 7/15 and this script shows both.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a water tank.
<bookmark mark='tap'/>In one hour, a tap fills seven tenths of the tank.
<bookmark mark='times'/>How much fills in one third, two thirds, three quarters and seven tenths of an hour?
<bookmark mark='full'/>And how long must the tap run to fill the whole tank?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.rule: the shaded tank is labelled one hour

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='look'/>Before multiplying, look for a top and a bottom with a common factor.
<bookmark mark='part'/>A part of an hour fills that same part of seven tenths.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 hour fills 7/10 of the tank; times 1/3, 2/3, 3/4, 7/10 of an hour

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one hour of the tap fills seven tenths of the tank.
<bookmark mark='times'/>The times are one third, two thirds, three quarters and seven tenths of an hour.

beats.on_screen: To find: the part filled in each time; the time to fill the whole tank

marks.find: the words To find and the two questions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the part filled in each time. We also find the time to fill the tank.

marks.rule: the rule is written as a time multiplied by seven tenths

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, the part filled is the time multiplied by seven tenths.

marks.a: the first product is written with the tops over the bottoms
marks.b: the second product is written as fourteen over thirty
marks.short: the fourteen and the thirty are linked by a line and divided by two

beats.colours: the shared factor in the accent colour
beats.moves_through: the 14 and the 30 change into 7 and 15
narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, one third times seven tenths is one times seven over three times ten. That is seven thirtieths.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Two thirds times seven tenths is fourteen thirtieths.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Fourteen and thirty share the factor two, so the part is seven fifteenths.

marks.c: the third product is written with the tops over the bottoms
marks.nof: a tick shows no top and bottom share a factor
marks.d: the fourth product is written with the tops over the bottoms

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step three, three quarters times seven tenths is three times seven over four times ten.
<bookmark mark='nof'/>No top and bottom share a factor, so that is twenty one fortieths.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Seven tenths times seven tenths is forty nine hundredths.

marks.seventh: the tank part for one seventh of an hour is written as a product
marks.short: the two sevens are linked by a line
marks.whole: ten parts of one tenth are counted, and the time is written as ten times one seventh

beats.colours: the shared factor in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='seventh'/>Step four, look at one seventh of an hour. The tap fills seven tenths times one seventh.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Seven and seven share the factor seven, so the tap fills one tenth of the tank.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>The whole tank needs ten such parts, and the time is ten times one seventh.

beats.on_screen: check: 3 × (1 × 7)/(3 × 10) = 7/10, the amount for one hour

marks.check: three copies of the first part are put back together
marks.match: the result is matched with the amount for one hour

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the first part. Three thirds of an hour make one hour.
<bookmark mark='match'/>Three times one times seven over three times ten shortens to seven tenths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (a) 7/30 (b) 7/15 (c) 21/40 (d) 49/100 of the tank; (e) 10/7 hours = 1 3/7 hours

marks.full: the time for the full tank is boxed with its unit
marks.mixed: the mixed number is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The parts filled are seven thirtieths and seven fifteenths. Then come twenty one fortieths and forty nine hundredths.
<bookmark mark='full'/>The full tank needs ten sevenths of an hour.
<bookmark mark='mixed'/>That is one and three sevenths hours.
